common_name: Superbena Pink Cashmere Verbena (Soft Pink-and-White Large-Flowered Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes in full sun to part sun with good air circulation; the soft coloring and huge flower umbels make it a standout spiller alongside Supertunia petunias in mixed containers.

directions: Superbena Pink Cashmere bears soft pink, silver, and white blooms held in unusually large, dense umbels that trial notes describe as rivaling Superbena Whiteout and Violet Ice in size. The mounding, trailing habit spreads readily as a groundcover or cascades to about 24 inches from a raised container or hanging basket, flowering continuously from planting until frost without deadheading. Grow in full to part sun (4 or more hours) in well-drained soil, watering when the top inch dries rather than keeping it constantly wet, since this Superbena line was bred to meet Proven Winners' highest powdery mildew resistance standard and stays clean through humid Gulf Coast summers that cause older trailing verbena to decline. Its gentle, blended coloring pairs especially well with deeper jewel-toned Superbena selections like Burgundy or Cobalt in the same bed or container, and the abundant, nectar-rich flower clusters draw bees and butterflies throughout the season while resisting deer browsing.

common_name: Superbena Stormburst Verbena (Purple-and-White Striped Bicolor Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes in full to part sun; expect individual flowers or whole branches to occasionally revert to solid violet or solid white, a normal novelty trait of this striped selection rather than a disease symptom.

directions: Superbena Stormburst produces striped bicolor flowers splashed with purple and white in each umbel, a novelty patterning that sets it apart from the solid-colored Superbena selections already common in the trade. Growth is very vigorous and strongly trailing, mounding 6-12 inches tall while spreading 18-30 inches and cascading up to 24 inches as a spiller in combination planters or hanging baskets. Grow in full to part sun (4 or more hours) in well-drained soil, letting the top inch dry between waterings; the plant is notably heat tolerant and holds its bloom quality through extreme summer heat that stalls many other bedding annuals. It flowers continuously from planting to frost without deadheading, attracts butterflies, resists deer browsing, and its high-contrast striping makes it a strong focal point among the more subtly toned Superbena and Superbena Royale colors already grown for Gulf Coast landscapes.

common_name: Superbena Violet Ice Verbena (White-Eyed Vibrant Purple Large-Flowered Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes in full sun (6 or more hours ideal) for the most vibrant purple coloring and the largest flower umbels; occasional individual flowers may shift to striped or solid white.

directions: Superbena Violet Ice bears vibrant purple flowers centered on a large, crisp white eye, giving each umbel strong two-tone contrast from a distance. The mounding-trailing habit spreads 18-30 inches and cascades up to 24 inches, functioning as a vigorous spiller in raised containers and hanging baskets or as fast-filling groundcover in beds. Grow in full to part sun in well-drained soil, allowing the top inch to dry between waterings; the selection is disease resistant and notably heat tolerant, holding both flower size and color intensity through peak Gulf Coast summer heat. It blooms continuously from planting to frost without deadheading, attracts butterflies, resists deer, and its exceptionally large flowers and umbels make it a benchmark size reference among newer Superbena introductions.

common_name: Superbena Royale Romance Verbena (Early-Blooming Burgundy-Red Large-Flowered Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated transplants after last hard frost danger passes in full to part sun; Romance is bred to bloom earlier in the season and finish well in smaller containers than standard Superbena varieties, patented as USPP 29,013.

directions: Superbena Royale Romance bears rich burgundy-red flowers in the large, dense umbels typical of the Superbena Royale line, offering a deeper, wine-toned alternative to the classic Superbena Burgundy already common in the trade. Its habit is vigorous and mounded rather than strongly trailing, though stems will spill over container edges, reaching 6-12 inches tall and spreading 18-24 inches. It blooms notably earlier in the season than standard Superbena selections and finishes well even in smaller pots, making it a strong choice for early-spring retail color as well as summer landscape beds. Grow in full to part sun in well-drained soil, letting the soil dry out a little between waterings; the plant is heat tolerant, deer resistant, and flowers continuously from planting to frost without deadheading, attracting butterflies throughout the season.
